scope: Proposition E.10 (The full invariant step) of the manuscript “Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width” (preprints/Positive-scalar-curvature-and-uniform-codimension-two-width-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 336 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f67c30579306bd4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 95-96. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the stage r invariant and the conclusion of Theorem D.6. For every nonempty parent packet of base dimension at least two, processing j0 produces the compatible smooth split packets of Theorem A.1, with the required forced signs and continuous projection maps. There are smooth compatible old metrics and 399 new torus factors 95 on every packet such that the profiles, cores, potentials, and scalar curvature satisfy the stage r + 1 invariant. This includes a possible one-dimensional output, on which the scalar lower bound is global. After the radial split the packets have the complete compact-part/product-end geometry of Theorem A.2.
